# Amendments Functions

Reusable functions for proposing a replacement at a permitted document path and applying it after every configured approver has approved. There is one pending proposal at a time. These functions define callable behavior; they do not themselves establish a caller’s permission or an automatic trigger.

## Configuration and state

- `parameters.paths` lists the exact paths eligible for proposals.
- `parameters.approvers` identifies the channels permitted to propose and approve. Every listed channel must have an approval recorded before application.
- `bindings.state` supplies the document path holding amendment state; `bindings.editable` supplies the path whose value must equal `true` to record a proposal or approve a pending one. No concrete paths or configuration defaults are supplied here. Paths refer to the document where the functions execute.
- `clauseKey` supplies the `clause` value in emitted Domain Events.

`initialize` adds state at `bindings.state` with `revision: 1`, `proposal: {}` and `history: {}`, then returns `acceptedNew`. These are initialization values, not substitutes for missing state. `revision` is a version counter incremented when an amendment is applied. `proposal` stores `id`, `path`, `replacement`, the submission `revision`, and an `approvals` map keyed by channel. `history` records applied proposal identifiers with value `true`; it is not a full archive of proposal contents. An explicitly empty `proposal` means no pending proposal; absent state does not establish initialization or completion.

## Proposing

`propose` accepts `expectedRevision`, `path`, `proposalId` and `replacement`. The identifier must be nonempty text containing neither `/` nor `~`; `replacement` is the exact proposed replacement value. Optional `preservePending` defaults to `false`.

The actor comes from `call/channel` and must belong to `parameters.approvers`, otherwise the call fails with `APPROVER_REQUIRED`. `proposePublic` delegates to `propose` and retains this restriction. `recordProposal` delegates directly to the inherited recording helper without adding that actor check.

Recording rejects a mismatched revision (`STALE_REVISION`), an unlisted path (`FIELD_NOT_AMENDABLE`), an editable value other than `true` (`TERMS_FROZEN`), or an invalid identifier (`INVALID_PROPOSAL_ID`). After these checks:

- Reusing the pending identifier returns `duplicate` only if replacement, path and revision match; otherwise it rejects with `PROPOSAL_ID_CONFLICT`.
- An identifier already present in `history` rejects with `PROPOSAL_ID_USED`.
- With `preservePending: true`, a different pending proposal rejects with `PROPOSAL_PENDING`. Otherwise the new proposal replaces it and starts with empty approvals.

Successful recording emits `Amendment Proposed` with `clause` and `proposalId`, and returns `acceptedNew`. It neither changes the target value nor counts the proposer as an approver.

## Approving and applying

`approve` takes a nonempty `proposalId` and requires an approver channel. An identifier marked `true` in `history` returns `duplicate` before pending-proposal and editability checks. Otherwise the identifier must match the pending proposal (`PROPOSAL_CHANGED`), and editing must still be enabled (`TERMS_FROZEN`). An already-recorded approval then returns `duplicate`.

A new approval is recorded. Once all configured approvers have approved, the function replaces the stored proposal’s target with its replacement, marks its identifier in `history`, increments `revision`, clears `proposal`, and emits `Amendment Applied` with `clause` and `proposalId`.

`acceptedNew` can mean only that an approval was recorded; it does not by itself mean the amendment was applied. An attempted call is not a committed outcome. Approval does not repeat the proposal-time path or revision checks, so application relies on the stored proposal and the current approver configuration.
